newsitem.title: USA: Airborne Express to receive Boeing 767 in August.
newsitem.headline: Airborne Express to receive Boeing 767 in August.

text.p: Airborne Express said it will receive in August the first of 12 second-hand Boeing 767-200 aircraft acquired from Itochu Air Lease Corp and Marubeni Corp. It will be converted to Airborne Express' requirements.

The second 767-200 will arrive in October and this will be followed by four deliveries in 1998, four in 1999 and two in 2000. The agreement to acquire the 12 aircraft was signed in December 1995, it added.
The carrier expects the first two Boeing 767-200s to join its revenue service in the first quarter of 1998.
A company spokeswoman said cargo doors will not be installed in the new aircraft. Freight will be loaded through the passenger door using an adaptation of Airborne's patented cargo containers.
The company said a saving of about $1 million per plane will be made by not installing cargo doors on the newly-acquired aircraft.
Airborne Express is still considering a purchase of an additional 10-15 767-200 aircraft and said by 2004 it estimated spending $600 million on newly-acquired planes.
The approximate cost of the first 12 planes at $290 million, or $24.2 million per plane, includes modifications and support items, it added.
Airborne Express operates a fleet of 63 McDonnell Douglas DC-9s, 35 Douglas DC-8s, and 11 NAMC YS-11 aircraft.
